sense: a variety of things of one kind

terms.gloss: variety, a range of different things
evidence: Phaedr. 4 epil. 2: cōpiōsa abundat rērum varietās
Cic. Imp. Pomp. 14: varietāte frūctuum (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Properly of mixed colours, then of anything made up of unlike things (Cicero, Fin. 2.10).

terms.gloss: of every kind: a whole range of
evidence: Liv. 10.21.3: dīlēctum omnis generis hominum habērī jussit
terms.comment: The genitive of genus, kind (see kind).

phrases.latin: adhūc supersunt multa quae possim loquī, et cōpiōsa abundat rērum varietās
phrases.english: there is still much left that I could tell, and a rich range of material

phrases.latin: varietās enim Latīnum verbum est, idque propriē quidem in disparibus colōribus dīcitur, sed trānsfertur in multa disparia: varium poēma, varia ōrātiō, variī mōrēs, varia fortūna
phrases.english: for variety is a Latin word, and properly it is said of different colours, but it is carried over to many things that differ: a varied poem, varied speech, varied ways, varied fortune

sources: Lewis & Short: varietas · Lewis & Short: genus

Quotations from the Latinitas loci collections (loci-phaedrus), checked against the editions named there. Cicero, De finibus 2, and Livy 10 and 21 checked against the Perseus Latin texts (9 November 2026).
Citations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them and have not been checked against an edition.
